case_name: Gian Singh v. State of Punjab

pages.text:
REPORTABLE
IN THE SUPREME COURT OF INDIA
CRIMINAL APPELLATE JURISDICTION
SPECIAL LEAVE PETITION (CRL.) NO. 8989 OF 2010

GIAN SINGH ... PETITIONER
VERSUS
STATE OF PUNJAB AND ANOTHER ... RESPONDENTS

JUDGMENT

R.M. LODHA, J.

1. The question before this three-Judge Bench is whether the High Court has the power under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 (CrPC) to quash criminal proceedings in non-compoundable offences where the parties have settled the dispute amicably.

2. In our considered view, the power of the High Court in quashing a criminal proceeding or FIR under Section 482 of the Code is distinct from the power of a criminal court for compounding the offences under Section 320 of the Code. Inherent power under Section 482 is of wide plenitude with no statutory limitation but must be exercised with circumspection to secure the ends of justice.

3. In cases of offences arising from commercial, financial, mercantile, civil, partnership or such like transactions, or offences arising out of matrimony relating to dowry, etc. or family disputes where the wrong is basically private or personal in nature and the parties have resolved their entire dispute, High Court may quash the criminal proceedings if continuation would be an abuse of process of law.
